name: Engine Support Systems
summary: Everything that keeps the race LT engine alive but is not the long block: dry-sump lubrication, engine coolant circuit, the LT4 supercharger low-temp intercooler loop, FT3 fuel cell and surge-tank fuel delivery, induction, exhaust, breathers, and the front cooler stack. The ZL1 baseline is a WET-sump LT4 with a returnless PWM fuel system and an 11-heat-exchanger cooling package; the race build converts to a dry sump, a trunk-mounted FT3 cell with a surge tank and a constant ~72 psi low-side supply, long-tube headers and a fully ducted cooling stack.
overview:
Factory baseline. Contrary to a common assumption, the 6th-gen Camaro ZL1 LT4 is wet-sump (~10 qt, GM TechLink lists Camaro LT1/LT4 at 9.5 L / 10.0 qt of 0W-40); only the C7 Corvette Z51/Z06 LT engines got GM's factory dry sump. The ZL1 feeds its direct-injection high-pressure pump from a returnless, PWM-controlled in-tank pump (≈58 psi cruise / ≈72 psi WOT). Cooling is a large radiator plus a separate low-temperature loop (front heat exchanger, electric pump) for the supercharger's two intercooler bricks, and the track package adds engine oil, transmission and differential coolers.

Lubrication. Sustained road-race g-loads on slicks starve a wet sump, so the race build uses a billet dry-sump pan with 4-5 scavenge stages (one per crank-bay pair plus timing case), a belt-driven external pump with built-in pressure regulation, a de-aerating remote tank in the right front of the engine bay, a remote filter, a thermostatically controlled oil cooler in the right front corner, and -16/-12 AN plumbing. If the engine must stay wet-sump, run a trap-door baffle and an Accusump.

Cooling. Keep the engine circuit (radiator + pressurized surge/degas tank + 160-180 °F thermostat) and the LT4 intercooler loop completely separate. The IC heat exchanger sits first in the airflow. Duct every core so no air bypasses, vent the exit air through the hood, and use water + surfactant instead of glycol where the track bans antifreeze. Upgrading the IC heat exchanger and reservoir volume is the most effective cure for ZL1 heat soak.

Fuel. The factory saddle tank is removed and an FIA FT3 cell (e.g., Fuel Safe ED122B 22 gal / 19.3 usable) sits in a steel or aluminum can in the trunk behind the axle, behind a sealed bulkhead (NASA CCR 15.4.1.1; SCCA metal bulkhead). From 2026 NASA requires the cell to be entirely rearward of the seat rear mounts. FT3 certification expires 5 years after manufacture. A lift pump keeps a surge tank full; twin feed pumps in the surge tank supply a bypass regulator at the tank (short-loop return) so only one -8 line runs forward, under the passenger floor, to the engine-driven DI pump. Hold low-side pressure at ≈72 psi (not below 68 psi with a Lingenfelter big-bore DI pump).

Exhaust. Stainless long-tubes (1-7/8 in common, 2 in for big power) replace the ZL1 tri-Y manifolds; check dry-sump pump and steering-shaft clearance. Use V-band collectors, wideband O2 per bank, a 3 in X-pipe in the tunnel, flex joints, and race mufflers behind the axle (or side exits if rules/sound allow). Heat-shield the tunnel, floor and the trunk floor under the fuel cell.

Common failure points: dry-sump belt failure (carry spares, guard it), oil blowing out the tank breather (overfilled tank/undersized vent), fuel pressure drop in long corners (lift pump/pickup), expired or foam-degraded cells, cracked header flanges/loose header bolts, air trapped in the IC loop, and undersized or poorly ducted radiators.
buildNotes: Phase 1: weld fuel-cell cradle, strap anchors, rear bulkhead, oil-tank and cooler-stack brackets before paint; remove factory tank, EVAP and fuel lines.
Phase 2: install the fuel cell, surge tank, pumps, filters, regulator and run the single -8 feed line and vent lines while the chassis is bare.
Phase 5 (engine on stand): fit dry-sump pan, pump bracket, mandrel, pulleys, belt and pump fittings; verify pickup clearances; set up header clearance mock-up.
Phase 6: install engine/trans; confirm pan-to-ground and header clearances at race ride height.

Phase 7: install headers and exhaust from the front back; then oil tank, filter, thermostat, cooler and all -AN oil lines; then cooler stack, radiator, IC heat exchanger, pump and reservoir, all coolant hoses; then intake and breathers.
Phase 8: wire pumps and fans through the PDM with kill-switch and stall shutoff; add oil/fuel/coolant pressure and temperature sensors.

Phase 11: fill fuel and leak-check at pressure; prime oil system (ignition/fuel disabled) until pressure registers; vacuum-fill engine coolant and IC loop; first start, check leaks, bleed, re-torque header/clamps after heat cycle; set dry-sump tank level hot at idle.

schematics.title: Dry-sump oil circuit
schematics.description: Complete dry-sump path: crankcase is scavenged by 4 pump stages into the tank, de-aerated oil feeds the pressure stage, then filter → thermostat (→ cooler) → engine gallery. Tank vents to the catch can. Optional Accusump on the pressure side.

schematics.title: Engine coolant circuit (high-temp)
schematics.description: Water pump → block/heads → water outlet → upper hose → radiator → lower hose → thermostat housing → pump. Degas lines from the radiator and the engine high point feed the pressurized surge tank, whose make-up line returns solid coolant to the pump inlet. Heater core deleted with a bypass loop.

schematics.title: LT4 supercharger intercooler loop (low-temp)
schematics.description: Electric pump → supercharger intercooler bricks → reservoir (degas) → front heat exchanger → pump. Completely separate from the engine coolant circuit.

schematics.title: Fuel system (cell → surge → feed → DI pump)
schematics.description: Cell pickup → 100 µm pre-filter → lift pump → surge tank → twin feed pumps → 10 µm filter → bypass regulator (~72 psi) with short-loop return to the surge tank → single -8 feed line → bulkheads → engine dry-break → DI high-pressure pump (engine). Surge overflow returns to the cell; cell vents through a rollover valve.

schematics.title: Exhaust flow
schematics.description: Each bank: 4 primaries → collector → V-band → catted/test connection pipe (wideband O2) → X-pipe → flex → mid pipe → muffler → tip. Side-exit option branches after the X-pipe.

schematics.title: Air intake path & crankcase ventilation
schematics.description: Fascia snorkel → sealed air box → filter → MAF/IAT → intake tube → couplers → throttle body → LT4 supercharger. Crankcase/tank vapors go to the catch can; can vents to filter or the fresh-air port.

routes.name: Main feed: regulator → engine DI pump (-8)
